The Editors\
*Mathematics Education Research Journal*

Dear Editors,

We are submitting "Teacher Beliefs, School Context, and Reform-Oriented Teaching: A Bayesian Multilevel Study of Lower-Secondary Mathematics Teachers in China" for consideration as a full-length article in *Mathematics Education Research Journal*.

Reform of mathematics teaching commonly assumes that changing what teachers believe will change how they teach. The paper tests that assumption for connectionist practice, the reform-oriented teaching that builds on students' own mathematical understandings and connects mathematical ideas with one another. Using original questionnaire data from 155 lower-secondary mathematics teachers across 35 schools in Wenzhou, China, we relate teachers' equity beliefs and their school's socioeconomic position to self-reported connectionist practice in Bayesian multilevel models.

Two findings speak directly to mathematics teacher education. First, a general equity orientation was modestly associated with connectionist practice, whereas teachers' beliefs about mathematics, learners, and pedagogy showed no credible association once that orientation was accounted for. Read through belief system theory, the mathematics-specific beliefs appear peripheral to what these teachers do in the classroom. Second, the school's socioeconomic position carried more weight than beliefs where its association was credible, and its direction changed across year groups, which suggests that reform-oriented mathematics teaching depends on the conditions of the school as well as on the convictions of the teacher.

The analysis also shows how measurement uncertainty from item response models and missing-data uncertainty from imputation can be carried through to substantive conclusions, which may be useful to others working with modest samples of mathematics teachers.

The manuscript reports original data collected by the authors, is not under consideration elsewhere, and has been approved by both authors. The study received ethical approval from the University of Manchester Research Ethics Committee.

We look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,

Chi Zhang\
on behalf of the authors
